To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
axonal transport is a key cellular process for the function and maintenance of a neuron and its defects play a critical role in the pathophysiology of AD.

AD-linked pathogenic factors respectively perturb four basic components of axonal transport through different signaling pathways, and these factors act in an overlapping and synergistic way to cause axonal transport defects.
AD-related pathologic factors perturb AT through multiple pathways, and MT-stabilizing agents and alteration in the phosphotransferases activities may represent a novel therapeutic strategy for AD.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of AT defects in AD and provides a theoretical basis for developing new therapeutic strategies.
the molecular mechanisms of AD, which may help to understand the pathogenesis of AD and develop new therapeutic approaches for the treatment of AD.
the role of AT defects in AD pathogenesis, and the possible therapeutic strategies targeting AT.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
AD is a “disease of axonal transport”.
the AT defects in AD are a complex, multifactorial, and multilevel process.

AD-linked pathologic agents perturb the four components of AT to cause AT defects, and the AT defects in AD are the result of the overlapping, synergistic and circulating effects of the four components.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
AT defects in AD are not only a consequence but also a cause of AD pathology.
the AD pathology, including Aβ, hyperphosphorylated tau and other factors, causes AT defects via multiple pathways, which is an important mechanism for the development of AD.
the AT defects are the key factors in AD pathology and therapeutic strategies targeting AT could be promising in AD treatment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AT system is an attractive target for therapeutic intervention of AD.
AT defects may serve as a potential target for AD treatment.
AD-linked pathologic proteins perturb AT through various mechanisms, which may be a common pathway for AD pathogenesis.
